newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Avonmmore seeks to create single share.
newsitem.headline: Avonmmore seeks to create single share.

text.p: Irish food group Avonmore Food Plc said it is calling a shareholders meeting on December 16 to remove the formal distinction between its A and B ordinary shares and simplify the group's capital structure.
It said in a statement that the purpose will be to create a single class or ordinary share.
There are 74.7 million A shares quoted on the Dublin and London exchanges while 100,000,000 B shares are unquoted and the entire B issue is held by parent company Avonmore Creameries.
The A and B shares have different nominal values of 0.05 and 0.20 Irish pounds respectively, the company said.

The company proposes to create a single class of share by Avonmore Creameries exchanging its B shares for the same number of A shares with the 15 pence difference being credited to the share premium account.
All the ordinary A shares will then be redesignated as ordinary shares of five pence each.
An application will be made to have the new shares issued listed on the Dublin and London exchanges, the company said.
The voting strength of existing holders of A shares will not be affected in any way, it said.
